catalog.summary: One goal-scoped requirement preserves existing missing-person cases and area-watch consequences in headless JSON debriefs. Current code inspection must establish existing behavior, serialization gaps and compatibility constraints; no implementation status is inferred from the code index.

coverage.reason: Core gameplay and world rules are outside this serialization goal. Exact replay is supporting context for the §08 requirement, not a separate task.
Resource accounting, travel and chains are outside scope; existing consequence values must be preserved, not recalculated.
Operative abilities, movement and recruitment do not belong to the requested debrief serialization change.
People, ties, fear and Standing provide upstream consequences. Changing their rules or between-mission processing is outside this goal.
Missing-person alarms and security responses are upstream simulation behavior. This goal preserves their existing debrief consequences without modifying detection, dispatch or the response dial.
Combat, takedown costs and Heat are outside scope; no new consequence calculations are requested.
Handover's missing-person route is useful inspection context, but mission rules and route implementation are outside the serialization goal.
Defines the missing-person cases, area watch and district-security consequences that the headless JSON debrief must preserve.
Generation and mission checking are outside scope. Replay consistency supports the §08 acceptance criteria without requiring a separate generator task.
Presentation and other query APIs are unrelated to this specific JSON debrief goal.
Shared-engine architecture and replay constrain verification of §08; engine migration, performance work and milestone delivery are outside scope.
Crew workflow and historical decisions are context only. Relevant case decisions corroborate §08 and do not create another serialization requirement.
Uncoached playtests and presentation gates do not verify the requested headless serialization contract.
Role ownership and replay expectations are design context, not additional work for this goal.
Art, assets, lighting and visual presentation are explicitly excluded and unrelated to JSON debrief preservation.

requirements.title: Preserve existing case and area-watch consequences in JSON debriefs
requirements.quote: | missing persons and cases [S] | each open case; the area watch: +1 posted guard and +1 camera on the block where the person was last seen, for 3 missions; the district's security level S | a kill never found: +2 T, no Menace, close ties fear +1, the case stays open until the body is found · a found killing: −1 Standing, grief, its case closes after 3 missions · every 2 open cases raise S by 1, at most +2 |
acceptance: Inspect the current debrief model, consequence calculation, JSON writer and consumers to establish which case and area-watch data already exist and which are omitted from JSON. Treat the code index and prior reviews as navigation only.

Serialize existing missing-person and case consequences without losing their existing identities, status, affected locations or associated values. Preserve the existing area-watch additions, duration and district security level wherever represented by the current debrief model.

For existing scenarios covering an undiscovered killing and a found killing, JSON faithfully represents the computed consequences. Do not introduce or change Trail, Standing, fear, case closure, area-watch duration or security-level calculations.
Repeated serialization of the same debrief produces byte-identical JSON. Replaying the same starting state and orders produces identical serialized case and area-watch consequences.
Serialization does not advance time, mutate simulation or debrief state, change checksums, apply consequences again or alter subsequent simulation behavior.

Preserve existing JSON fields, types and meanings and compatibility with current consumers. Verify both debriefs with consequences and debriefs without them; establish any additive representation from current contract inspection rather than inventing field names during extraction.

Do not implement campaign persistence or new consequence rules. Flag absent model data, unspecified rulebook values or conflicts with the quoted design as inspection blockers instead of supplying invented defaults.
requirements.rationale: Makes existing campaign consequences available to headless consumers without changing gameplay. A bounded serialization change should be modest, but omitted model data and consumer compatibility require inspection. Determinism follows §01 and §11; the explicit goal adds side-effect-free serialization and compatibility constraints. The human debrief passage 23452dd13fc8b530fd20ce15 supplies surrounding context but does not replace this literal §08 case row.
